svg.text: You type 5 commands. You stop at 5 gates. Everything in between runs on its own.
AGENT — a worker with its own memory. Does one job, hands back one file, then forgets everything
REVIEWER — can read but never write
LEVEL 1 — THE WHOLE THING AT A GLANCE
how will we know it works?
Write it, test it, review it,
check it on the real site.
HOW CAREFUL TO BE — four lanes, same five blocks, joined at different points
STANDARD changing something that exists → /spec --amend (one paragraph) → /build ×N → /ship
If the change shows on a screen, G4 is compulsory — even for TRIVIAL.
And a safety net: if a TRIVIAL change turns out to touch the database or
login, a hook blocks it and makes you re-triage. Triage guesses; the hook checks.
LEVEL 2 — WHAT EACH BLOCK READS, DOES, AND WRITES
a slug is a short nickname —
and the branch, so nothing drifts.
ends at 🚦 G1 — you read it
Linear · old session logs · the code
That's all it needs to start.
1 the researcher agent gathers everything already decided
2 it shows you that, so your scope cut is informed
3 one conversation: what's IN and OUT for v1 first,
then what happens at the edges, then how we'll know it works
You describe what you want in plain words. Tables, migrations and how it's stored are NOT your problem here — that's /design, two stages later.
become the tests, and what G4
ends at 🚦 G2 — you pick one
1 builds 2–3 versions that look genuinely different, plain HTML
2 you open them and choose. Never the agent — this is taste
Spec first, always. A prototype with no scope cut grows the feature —
one thing leads to another. Inside the fence, it can only explore.
how data is stored — all here.
decision, then only the ones that overlap
An ADR is a written-down decision:
what we chose, what we turned
1 researcher — which approaches exist, what each one costs
2 writes the decision, opening in plain English: what each
option means for the product · what it costs to undo later ·
how the industry normally does it · one recommendation
3 adr-checker — does it meet the spec? a better option missed?

text.tspan: does it contradict a decision we made months ago?

svg.text: 4 tickets — INVEST-checked, sized S/M/XS (>M → split), EARS criteria, each saying what it waits on
break, e.g. "a buyer can never see
another buyer's list". If a machine
can check it, it becomes a test.
Only ONE of the ten agents can
write code: the builder. The rest
can only read — enforced by the
tools they're given, not by asking.
ends at 🚦 G4 — you see it run
get file paths and one question.
1 plan — exactly which files, which function names, real test code
2 plan-checker — will this plan actually get there? cheapest check
3 test-writer — failing tests, written from the SPEC, never the code
4 builder — writes the code until the tests pass
5 test-runner — runs them. Can't edit, so it can't "fix" a test
6 reviewers, all at once — critic always · security if it touches the
database or login · consistency if a new component or pattern
appeared — "did it reuse ours, or invent and patch?"
7 visual-verifier — opens the real page and photographs it
If it gets stuck: 2 tries on failing
separately. Then it stops and says what
it thinks is wrong with the instruction.
The builder can disagree. It may refuse
a finding in writing — you settle it at G4.
ends at 🚦 G5 — on the real site
1 rebase onto dev FIRST — pull in Ayush's work before verifying,
instead of verifying your branch and hoping nothing moves
2 re-run the whole suite on the rebased code. Touched a tested
or visible file? → back to G4 · 2 rounds max, then it stops
4 walk every criterion on the live URL yourself
Buy and Sales Calendar were both
done. A ticket closes on live
evidence, or it does not close.
1 make it happen again on purpose — from facts, not guesses
2 test-writer writes a test that fails for exactly that reason
3 hand it to /build, which makes that test pass
A fix with no failing test first is a guess that happened to compile.
That test is what stops the same
bug coming back in six months,
LEVEL 3 — WHERE EVERYTHING IS KEPT FITS THE FOLDERS THAT ALREADY EXIST — no renames, no new tree (R7: "fit it, don't replace it")
├─ architecture/adr/ ADR-INDEX.md one line per decision
└─ muskan-build/0007-pricelist/ throwaway — archive when shipped · same number as its spec

what each stage wrote, and where
